newsitem.title: USA: Ohio voters reject 70 pct of proposed bond issues.
newsitem.headline: Ohio voters reject 70 pct of proposed bond issues.

text.p: Ohio voters shot down 69.8 percent of the $745 million of bond issues on the ballots Tuesday, according to the Ohio Municipal Advisory Council.
The council said $225 million, or 30.2 percent, of the total was approved.
The results represented a turnabout from 1995's voting trend, in which 75.7 percent of the $678 million on the ballot won approval.
The largest issue approved was a $61.9 million Dublin City School District issue, okayed by a vote of 13,825 to 11,659.
The largest item defeated was a $44 million Lebanon City School District issue, rejected by a vote of 5,683 to 3,880.
